reasoning_traces.think:
The PlayerCard primitive encodes a set of time-normalized performance indicators that form a compact feature space for predictive modeling. Each statistic—such as targets per game or rushing yards per game—is a derived quantity from raw play-level data. These aggregates enable GSI to compute posterior distributions over expected outcomes using Bayesian updating techniques. The headline statistic acts as a summary measure, while the per-game aggregates provide granular detail for regression-based forecasting models. The inclusion of rank introduces ordinality useful for ordinal logistic regression or ranking algorithms. Failure modes arise when insufficient sample size leads to noisy estimates or when external factors like injury disrupt normal performance trends. Dualities emerge between offensive and defensive roles where similar statistics can be interpreted differently depending on context.
